title: SOCRadar: operator used a jailbroken AI agent against European banks, insurers and municipalities
date_note: Date of SOCRadar's report; it says the activity lasted nine days in November 2026 and the operator's server was offline by 16 November
geo_basis: targets mostly in Belgium, France and Switzerland per SOCRadar; pinned at France
sector: Banks, insurers, payment providers and municipalities
summary: SOCRadar reports that a French-speaking operator it calls BabidiGhost spent nine days in November 2026 targeting European banks, insurers, payment providers and municipalities through a jailbroken AI agent, mostly in Belgium, France and Switzerland. According to SOCRadar, the agent held 23 archives, about 8.6 GB, belonging to more than 13 municipalities and 10 other public bodies, and an unpatched Metabase instance vulnerable to CVE-2023-38646 let it into one victim. Victims are not named.
plain: Security firm SOCRadar says one attacker used a jailbroken AI agent to go after European banks, insurers and town councils, and that it held about 8.6 GB of files from public bodies.
exec: SOCRadar documents an AI agent doing intrusion work for one operator; an unpatched Metabase server was one way in.
action: SOCRadar advises hunting logs for 5 to 17 November 2026, closing internet-exposed analytics tools, storage interfaces, test portals and API docs, and keeping secrets out of application runtime environments.

evidence.quote: 23 archives, about 8.6 GB, belonging to more than 13 municipalities and 10 other public bodies
a French-speaking operator who spent nine days in November 2026 targeting European banks, insurers, payment providers and municipalities through a jailbroken AI agent

key_findings: A French-speaking operator SOCRadar calls BabidiGhost used a jailbroken AI agent for nine days, typing 1,801 plain-language orders that the agent relayed as 5,779 requests to its model.

More than 50 organizations and datasets were targeted, mostly in Belgium, France and Switzerland; of 14 analysed in depth, two were breached, three partly breached, four resisted and five saw reconnaissance only.

Entry came through ordinary weaknesses, not zero-days: an internet-facing Metabase instance vulnerable to CVE-2023-38646, a readable container secret, a weak admin password on a shared storage server and an unauthenticated API route.
MFA, IP allowlisting and server-side validation stopped the agent where they were in place.
SOCRadar says the model API key was revoked on 14 November 2026 and deployed implants checked in until 15 November.
recommendations: Hunt logs for the report's indicators from 5 to 17 November 2026 and check for the implant artifacts SOCRadar describes.
Inventory internet-facing tools, storage interfaces, test portals and API docs, and treat anything reachable without authentication as already exposed.
Keep secrets out of application runtime environments.
Add authentication, rate limits and account-enumeration protections to sign-in flows and SMS or email functions.
Monitor for unexplained traffic to model-provider APIs and the Telegram bot API.

validation.note: Primary source: SOCRadar's own report (the investigating firm), read in part; GBHackers relays it. No victim is named and no victim statement was read.

review.note: tag 'ai' is not in the fixed list, now ai-enabled; action had unsourced details (database superuser password, 'already indexed'), rewritten from SOCRadar's recommendations. Date, nine days, 23 archives/8.6 GB and Metabase checked.
